Rashi on Yevamot 37a:10:1.hebrew: ראשון - דספק הוה, ראוי להיות כהן גדול ממה נפשך:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:10:1.english: The first [child] - Who is of uncertain [paternity], is fit to be a High Priest either way.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:10:2.hebrew: והשני - אם קיימה עד שילדה לו בן, ודאי ממזר מספק, שמא ראשון בן המת הוה, וקאי עליה בכרת, ואישתכח האי שני ולד חייבי כריתות וממזר:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:10:2.english: And the second - If he kept her [as his wife] until she bore him a son, [the child is] certainly a mamzer due to uncertainty, lest the first [child] was the son of the deceased, and [thus] he stood under [the prohibition of] karet regarding her, and this second [child] turns out to be the offspring of [a union] liable to karet, and a mamzer.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:11:1.hebrew: מאי קאמר - ר"א בן יעקב היכי מצי לאפוקי מספק ממזר:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:11:1.english: What is [he] saying - How can Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov remove [him] from [the status of] an uncertain mamzer?

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:11:2.english: Abaye said, etc., he is an uncertain mamzer and is prohibited to a mamzeret - And [also] to a fit [Israelite woman].

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:11:3.hebrew: ר"א אומר אין ממזר מספק אלא כודאי ממזר הוי ומותר בממזרת - דקסבר ספיקן בודאן מותר:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:11:3.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: He is not a mamzer out of doubt; rather, he is like a definite mamzer, and he is permitted [to marry] a mamzeret - For he holds [that] an uncertain [mamzer] is permitted [to marry] a definite [mamzer].

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:12:1.hebrew: ושני ממזר ודאי הוי מספק - כלומר, מתוך ספק זה נעשה כודאי ממזר ומותר בממזרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:12:1.english: And the second [child] is a definite mamzer due to uncertainty - That is to say, on account of this uncertainty, he becomes like a definite mamzer and is permitted [to marry] a mamzeret.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:13:1.hebrew: וקמיפלגי - אביי ורבא, דמר מוקי רבי אליעזר בן יעקב להיתירא ומר מוקי ליה לאיסורא, פליגי בדרבי אליעזר:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:13:1.english: And they disagree - Abaye and Rava, for one establishes Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov [as ruling] permissively and one establishes him [as ruling] prohibitively, disagree regarding [the statement of] Rabbi Eliezer.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:13:2.hebrew: ודאן בספיקן אסור - שמא הספק כשר הוא, ונמצא בא ממזר בקהל. וכן ספק ממזר בספק ממזרת, דשמא זה פסול וזה כשר:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:13:2.english: Their certain [ones] with their uncertain [ones] is prohibited - Lest the uncertain [person] is fit, and it turns out [that] a mamzer enters the congregation; and similarly, an uncertain mamzer with an uncertain mamzeret, for perhaps this one is unfit and that one is fit.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:14:1.english: Shetuki - [A child] who calls [for] his father, and his mother silences him.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:14:2.english: A foundling - [One] who was gathered in from the marketplace. And in all of them, there is [reason] to suspect lest [the mother] conceived from an unfit [man].

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:14:3.hebrew: כותי - אין מקפיד על קידושי כסף ושטר, דלית ליה גזירה שוה דקיחה קיחה, וכי מקדש חד, מנסבא לאידך. לפיכך כולן ספק ממזרים הם, שמא נתקדשה אמו לאחר:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:14:3.english: A Kuti [Samaritan] - He is not particular about betrothal by money or a document, for he does not accept the verbal analogy [gezerah shavah] of "taking" [and] "taking"; and when one [man] betroths [a woman], she marries another. Therefore, all of them are possible mamzerim, lest his mother had been betrothed to another [man].

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:15:1.hebrew: כי אמריתה - רב יהודה מסיים למילתיה ואזיל: כי אמריתה להא שמעתא דרב אמר הלכה כר"א קמיה דשמואל, אמר לי כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:15:1.english: When I said it - Rav Yehuda is continuing and concluding his statement: "When I said this teaching — that Rav said the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar — before Shmuel, he said to me, etc."

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:15:2.hebrew: נתיני - גבעונים שנתגיירו בימי יהושע בערמה, ויש בהן צד עבדות, דכתיב (יהושע ט׳:כ״ז) "ויתנם יהושע חוטבי עצים ושואבי מים לעדה":
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:15:2.english: Netinei - Gibeonites who converted in the days of Joshua through trickery, and they have an aspect of servitude, as it is written (Joshua 9:27): "And Joshua made them hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation."

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:15:3.hebrew: וכולן מותרין לבא זה בזה - אי אמרת ספיקן בודאן מותר, וכ"ש ספיקן בספיקן, היינו דמשכחת ליה כולן מותרין זה בזה: כהנים, לוים וישראלים מותרין זה בזה. לויי וישראלי, חללי, גירי וחרורי — עבדים משוחררים — מותרים זה בזה. גירי וחרורי, ממזרי ונתיני, שתוקי ואסופי מותרים זה בזה, דקהל גרים לא איקרי קהל, לפיכך ממזרים מותרים בהן. וכסדר הזה שנויים בקדושין (דף סט.):
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:15:3.english: And all of them are permitted to marry one another - If you say that their uncertain [cases are permitted to marry] their certain [cases], and all the more so their uncertain [cases] with their uncertain [cases], this is how you find [that] "all of them are permitted [to marry] one another": Priests, Levites, and Israelites are permitted [to marry] one another. Levites and Israelites, ḥalallim, converts, and ḥarurei — [meaning] freed slaves — are permitted [to marry] one another. Converts and freed slaves, mamzerim and netinim, shetukei and foundlings are permitted [to marry] one another, for a congregation of converts is not called "a congregation [of the Lord]," [and] therefore mamzerim are permitted [to marry] them. And in this order they are taught in Kiddushin (69a).

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:16:1.hebrew: ואת אמרת הלכה כר"א - שאין ממזר מותר בשתוקי, ולא שתוקי בשתוקי, ולא שתוקי באסופי (א"כ, לא משכחת לה כולהו מעורבים):
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:16:1.english: And you said [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar - [who holds] that a mamzer is not permitted [to marry] a shetuki, nor a shetuki [to marry] a shetuki, nor a shetuki [to marry] an asufi (if so, you do not find [that] all of them are intermingled).

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:1:1.english: In the evening Rava stated this - As you say.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:1:2.english: In the morning he retracted - And I heard from his mouth that she does not perform chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:2:1.hebrew: הכא מאי - לר' יהושע בריה דרב אידי קבעי לה:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:2:1.english: Here, what [is the law] - [He] asks this of Rabbi Yehoshua, son of Rav Idi.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:2:2.hebrew: מי עביד רבנן תקנתא לכהן - דאע"ג דלישראל בעינן יוציא בגט עד שיגיע זמנו, התם הוא דלכשיגיע זמנו מצי לאהדורה, אבל הכא, דאי מגרש לה לא מצי מהדר לה, תסגי בהפרשה בעלמא:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:2:2.english: Did the Sages enact an ordinance for a priest - For although for an Israelite we require [that] he divorce [her] with a bill of divorce until his time arrives, that is [only] there, where when his time arrives he can take her back; but here, where if he divorces her he cannot take her back, would mere separation suffice?

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:3:1.english: We act in accordance with [the opinion of] the Rabbis - And we rely on the offspring.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:5:1.english: He betrothed her within three [months] - [I.e.,] any widow or divorcee.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:5:2.hebrew: עירוקיה מסתייה - לא בעי למיכפייה דלכתוב גט, דגלי דעתיה דלא בעי לכנוס עד זמנו:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:5:2.english: His flight is sufficient for him - It is not necessary to compel him to write a bill of divorce, for he has revealed his intention that he does not wish to marry [her] until the [proper] time.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:6:1.hebrew: ורוב נשים לט' ילדן - ולייתי חטאת, דודאי בר קמא הוא, ואשת אח בת בנים בעל:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:6:1.english: And the majority of women give birth at nine [months] - And let him bring a sin-offering, for [the child] is certainly the son of the first [husband], and he has cohabited with [his] brother's wife who has children.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:8:1.english: And this [woman], since her fetus was not recognizable after a third of her days - For if it had been recognizable, we would not be in doubt.

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:8:2.english: After a third of her days - As it is written: "And it came to pass about three months [later]" (Genesis 38:24).

Rashi on Yevamot 37a:8:3.hebrew: איתרע לה רובא - דלא תשדייה בתר רוב נשים, אלא ספק בתר מיעוט, ספק בתר רוב:
Rashi on Yevamot 37a:8:3.english: [The presumption of] the majority is compromised for her - For you do not assign her [to follow] the majority of women; rather, [it is] uncertain [whether she follows] the minority, [or] uncertain [whether she follows] the majority.

Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:10:1.hebrew: ראשון ראוי להיות כה"ג - והא דאמר בפ"ק דכתובות (דף יג: ושם) גבי עשר כהנים שפירש אחד מהן ובעל, הולד שתוקי שמשתקין אותו מדין כהונה דבעינן זרעו מיוחס אחריו — לקמן בפ' נושאין (יבמות דף ק:) פריך לה, ומשני: זרעו מיוחס אחריו דרבנן; וכי גזור רבנן בזנות, בנישואין לא גזור:
Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:10:1.english: The first [child] is fit to become a High Priest - And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says in the first chapter of Ketubot (13b, and there) regarding ten priests, one of whom separated [from the group] and cohabited [with a woman], [that] the offspring is a shetuki, whom we silence from the law of priesthood because we require [that] "his seed is traced after him" — later, in the chapter [entitled] Nos'in (Yevamot 100b), [the Gemara] raises this difficulty and answers: [The requirement that] "his seed is traced after him" is rabbinic; and when the Rabbis decreed [this], [it was] in [a case of] licentiousness; in [a case of] marriage, they did not decree [it].

Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:18:1.hebrew: סבר לה כרב דאמר הלכה כר' אלעזר - והא דפריך בעשרה יוחסין (קידושין דף עג. ושם) גבי הא דאמר רבא: דבר תורה כו' שתוקי כשר, אלא מעתה שתוקי שתוקית לא ישא — לאו משום דלרבא שרי שתוקי בשתוקית, אלא משום דגם אליבא דרבנן אמר רבא מילתיה דהתם; להכי פריך, דלרבנן נמי שתוקי שתוקית לא ישא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:18:1.english: [Rava] holds in accordance with Rav, who said [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar - And as for that which [the Gemara] asks in [the chapter] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 73a and there), regarding that which Rava said, "By Torah law, etc., a shetuki is fit," [asking:] "If so, a male shetuki should not marry a female shetuki" — [this is] not because according to Rava a male shetuki is permitted to [marry] a female shetuki, rather because Rava stated his teaching there even according to the Rabbis; therefore [the Gemara] asks [this], for according to the Rabbis as well, a male shetuki may not marry a female shetuki.

Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:2:1.hebrew: מי עביד רבנן תקנתא או לא - בעיא זו אליבא דרבנן ולא אליבא דר' מאיר. ומכאן מדקדק בה"ג ובשאלתות, דהא דאמר בפ' אע"פ (כתובות דף ס: ושם) דהלכה כר"מ בגזרותיו — היינו דוקא בגזרותיו ולא בקנסותיו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:2:1.english: Did the Sages enact an ordinance or not? - This inquiry is according to the Rabbis, and not according to Rabbi Meir. And from here, Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot and [the author of] the She'iltot infer that that which is stated in the chapter [entitled] Af Al Pi (Ketubot 60b and there), that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir in his decrees — that is specifically regarding his decrees, and not regarding his penalties.

Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:9:1.hebrew: אי כל היולדת כו' - כה"ג דייק ברפ"ב דכתובות (דף טז:) גבי "כל הנישאת בתולה יש לה קול" כו', ובפ' המפלת (נדה דף כט.) גבי "כל היולדות מטנפות". אבל בפרק ואלו טריפות (חולין דף נג.) גבי "כל הדורס אין צפרנו נשמטת" לא דייק, (אע"ג) ד"כל" לאו דוקא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:9:1.english: "If every [woman] who gives birth, etc." - [The Gemara] makes a similar inference at the beginning of the second chapter of Ketubot (16b) regarding [the statement], "Every [woman] who is married as a virgin has a public report, etc.," and in the chapter [entitled] Hamapelet (Niddah 29a) regarding [the statement], "All [women] who give birth discharge [blood]." However, in the chapter [entitled] Ve'eilu Tereifot (Chullin 53a) regarding [the statement], "Any [predator] that claws, its claw does not detach," it does not make [this] inference, (even though) "all" is not meant literally.

Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:9:2.hebrew: רוב היולדת לט' כו' - וא"ת: מה מועיל המתנת ג' חדשים משום הבחנה? אכתי יכול לבא לידי ספק אם תנשא מיד ותלד לו' חדשים ויום אחד או אפילו ג' ימים, דיש להסתפק אם הוא בנו של ראשון ולא נקלט הזרע עד יום ג', או הוא בנו של שני, דיולדת לשבעה יולדת למקוטעים. וזהו תימה לומר שתהא האשה צריכה להמתין ג' חדשים וג' ימים, דלקמן משמע דג' חדשים דוקא, דאמר: "חוץ מיום שמת בו ויום שנתארסה בו". ואין לומר: כיון דהמתינה ג' חדשים שריא לינשא, ולא חיישינן שמא תלד משני לסוף ששה חדשים וב' ימים או ג', דסמכינן ארובא דלט' ילדן; וא"כ, דסמכינן ארובא דלט' ילדן, א"כ אפילו תוך ג' חדשים תנשא, דסמכינן ארובא, ואין צריך להמתין אלא חדש אחד, ושוב אין ספק — דאם תלד לסוף ט' ממיתת ראשון, אין להסתפק שמא הוא מז' לאחרון, דאזלינן בתר רוב נשים דלט' ילדן. אלא ע"כ כל מקום שיכול לבא לידי ספק החמירו חכמים. וי"ל דכ"כ לא היה משתהא הכרת העובר של ראשון עד שליש ימיה מן השני:
Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:9:2.english: In the majority of cases, [a woman] who gives birth after nine [months], etc. - And if you ask: What does waiting three months accomplish for the sake of distinguishing [the child's paternity]? Still, it can come to a doubt if she marries immediately [afterward] and gives birth at six months and one day, or even three days [into the second marriage], for there is room to be in doubt whether it is the son of the first [husband] and the seed was not absorbed until the third day, or it is the son of the second [husband], since [a woman] who gives birth at seven [months] gives birth to incomplete [months]. And it would be astonishing to say that the woman must wait three months and three days, for later [in the tractate] it is implied that [it is] three months specifically, as it says: "excluding the day on which he died and the day on which she was betrothed." And one cannot say [that] once she has waited three months she is permitted to marry, and we are not concerned lest she give birth from the second [husband] at the end of six months and two or three days because we rely on the majority [of women] who give birth at nine [months]; for if so, that we rely on the majority who give birth at nine [months], then she should be permitted to marry even within three months, since we rely on the majority, and she would need to wait only one month, and then there is no doubt — for if she gives birth at the end of nine [months] from the death of the first [husband], there is no room to be in doubt lest it is from seven [months] of the latter [husband], since we follow the majority of women who give birth at nine [months]. Rather, perforce, wherever it can come to a doubt, the Sages were stringent. And one can say that the recognition of the fetus from the first [husband] would not be delayed so long as until a third of her days from the second [husband].

Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:9:3.hebrew: וזו הואיל ולא הוכר - תימה, דאמאי לא מוקמינן לה בחזקת היתר ליבם, ולא יתחייב באשם תלוי, ויהא נמי ולד שני כשר? דסמוך מיעוט יולדת לשבעה אחזקה ואיתרע ליה רובא, ונסמוך ארובא דעוברה ניכר לשליש ימיה! דלעיל בפ' ד' אחין (יבמות דף ל:) חשבינן לה חזקה גבי ספק קידושין, ולקמן בפ' בתרא (יבמות דף קיט. ושם) אפילו היתה צרתה מעוברת חשבינן לה בחזקת זקוקה. וכ"ת דאיכא רובא אחרינא, דרוב נשים מתעברות ויולדות, לפיכך יש להחזיקה כמעוברת מן הראשון — דאין סברא כלל לומר בנשים ששהו עם בעליהן כמה שנים ולא עיברו ומתו בעליהם דרוב מעוברות; ולקמן (יבמות דף קיט.) הוא דאמר לה גבי האשה שהלך בעלה וצרתה למדינת הים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 37a:9:3.english: And this [woman], since [her fetus] was not recognized - It is astonishing: why do we not establish her on the presumption of being permitted to the yavam, so that he would not be liable for a suspensive guilt-offering, and the second child would also be fit? For combine the minority [of women who] give birth at seven [months] with the presumption, and the majority is weakened, and let us rely on the majority [of women] whose fetus is recognizable at a third of her days! For earlier, in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Aḥin (Yevamot 30b), we consider it a presumption regarding an uncertain betrothal; and later, in the last chapter (Yevamot 119a, and there), even if her co-wife was pregnant, we consider her to be on the presumption of being bound [to the yavam]. And if you say that there is another majority—that most women conceive and give birth, [and] therefore she should be presumed to be pregnant from the first [husband]—[that is not so,] for there is no sense at all in saying regarding women who stayed with their husbands for several years and did not conceive, and whose husbands [then] died, that most [of them] are pregnant; and it is later (Yevamot 119a) that [the Gemara] states this regarding [the Mishnah of] "The woman whose husband and co-wife went to a country overseas."
